newsitem.title: CHINA: China watchdog orders better stock risk control.
newsitem.headline: China watchdog orders better stock risk control.

text.p: China's top securities watchdog has ordered the two stock exchanges to investigate the risk control mechanisms of their members and told newspapers and magazines to report more on the risks of stock investment, the Shanghai Securities News said on Monday.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), in a circular, also banned encouragement of speculation in comments about the stock market "to prevent investors being misguided," the newspaper said.
The new instructions follow surges on the domestic A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen this year, with local media reporting that more than one million new investors had opened accounts.
"The exchanges must quickly organise several groups to investigate the risk control systems of their members and report the results to the CSRC," the newspaper quoted the circular as saying.
"All designated newspapers and magazines must strengthen reporting of laws and regulations concerning the stock market and comprehensively introduce the risks of stock investment," the circular said.
"Any comments on stock markets must not encourage speculation in order to prevent investors being misguided," it said.
The CSRC also ordered all securities houses and brokerages to display in their business halls information about the risk of trading on the stock markets.
Local securities watchdogs must check if securities institutions have displayed the information and report the results to the CSRC.
The CSRC will punish those who failed to display the information, the circular said but did not give details of the punishments.

Shanghai's A share market has risen more than 100 percent and its Shenzhen counterpart more than 250 percent since the start of this year after Beijing stressed the need to continue to develop the nation's stock markets.
The surging markets have attracted more and more local investors, with the number of China's stock investors growing to more than 20 million, the official media has reported.

The surges apparently have been beyond the expectations of the securities authorities and, to cool the over-heated markets, the CSRC has over the past few weeks issued a series of new rules and punished many brokerages for irregularities.
